messages:
eli (customer): Hey team — overnight batch for tenant `acme-inc` started failing ~02:10 UTC with a bunch of 503s and elevated p95. Seen a matching billing jump for that window. Sample request ids: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0a1b2c3e, req_0a1b2c3f. Logs on our side show `upstream reset` and some truncated responses. Can you triage?

maya (support): Thanks @eli — sorry about this. Two quick asks so we can reproduce: 1) a representative curl that your batch runner uses (headers + body shape); 2) whether you're using streaming or non-streaming responses, and what concurrency/token targets the job uses. Also please collect the raw response bodies for those request ids if possible.

eli (customer): Here's a safe-ish example (we redacted API key):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-rlm-13b","input":"Summarize logs for window 02:00-02:20 UTC","max_tokens":1024, "stream":false}'
```
We run batches with concurrency 10 per worker, ~120 workers, token distribution: ~60% requests ~300 tokens, 30% ~1200, 10% ~2000. We do not use streaming.

sam (sre): Noted. @maya @eli — two things we'll want: the raw server-side `X-Request-Id` / response headers for the sample ids, and a HAR or tcpdump of a failing run if you can. If you can't capture a HAR, at minimum keep the full HTTP request/response (headers+body). Also: I see a deploy around 02:05 from the bot — might be correlated.

deploy-bot: Deployed open-rlm-13b:2026-02-14-02:05 UTC -- rollout id r-deploy-4421.

maya (support): Good call. @eli — please run `support-cli collect-debug` on your side to bundle client logs + request ids. Example command we recommend: 
```
support-cli collect-debug --tenant acme-inc --request-ids req_0a1b2c3d,req_0a1b2c3e,req_0a1b2c3f --include-har --include-req-resp --output debug-acme-1876543210.tar.gz
```
That will produce a tar we can ingest. If you can't run that, at least paste the exact curl request/response pair for one failing id including any `X-Request-Id` header from our API response.

eli (customer): Will run the collector now. One more oddity: billing reported 429s for a short window then later 503s — authorization token TTL is 1h and rotated, but we didn't rotate mid-run. Could rate-limit fallback be triggering a downstream fallback chain?

noah (eng-runtime): Possible. If clients start retrying aggressively on 429 with backoff disabled, that can create thundering retries that push through bursts and result in resource exhaustion and 503s. Can you confirm your retry policy? If it retries immediately 3x that could amplify.

eli (customer): Our runner has simple retry: 1 immediate retry on 5xx, exponential backoff for subsequent attempts. We do not retry on 429.

sam (sre): Ok. Next steps from us: once we receive the debug tar we'll: 1) correlate req ids to service-side traces, 2) check the runtime kernel metrics (queue lengths, active batch sizes), 3) validate whether the 02:05 rollout touched batching/kv-cache changes, 4) run a targeted replay in staging with the same concurrency/token mix.

maya (support): For the staging replay please provide a small prompt-set (10 prompts representative of your mix). Example format: one prompt per line in a `prompts.txt`. We'll run stress-replay like: 
```
stress-replay --prompts prompts.txt --concurrency 12 --workers 8 --token-buckets 300:60,1200:30,2000:10 --model open-rlm-13b --record-ids replay-run-1876543210
```
This produces a HAR + server trace ids we can map back.

eli (customer): Uploading debug-acme-1876543210.tar.gz to the support share now (link redacted). Also attaching `prompts.txt` (10 samples) and a small sample of request/response for req_0a1b2c3d.

maya (support): Got it — we pulled the tar. Running initial correlation now. Please avoid sharing PII in the bundle — we scrubbed obvious fields but if you see anything sensitive, redact and re-upload.

sam (sre): I'll spin up the replay in staging with the provided distribution and post p50/p95/p99 + error breakdown. If we reproduce, next step is narrow diff between runtime commit at r-deploy-4421 and previous tag.

eli (customer): Thanks all — will monitor and standby for next updates. Appreciate the quick coordination :heart:
